description: Employer-neutral record of defects that escaped review into a merged coordinator change, the escape budget that governs the conditional typed control-plane decision, and the gate observations that motivated it. Incidents are identified by this repository's own public commit hashes; no external identifiers, programme code names, or private review references appear here.

coverageWindow.notes: Gate 0 is the first coordinator-authored change merged into this repository (introduction of the reviewer agent). The window closes at the head this hardening layer is stacked on. Ten coordinator changes have been merged in the window; every incident below was found in deterministic execution because no shadow or live coordinator run has ever been performed.

categories.definition: The runtime bound a value to the wrong shape: a collection collapsed to a scalar or to null, a scalar was widened to a collection, or a collection was nested inside another collection. The logic was correct for the shape the author intended.
The intended shape was preserved but the computation, guard, or control flow was wrong, including state captured at the wrong time by a closure.
A model produced output that did not satisfy the contract the caller assumed: missing field, wrong envelope, prose where structured output was required, or a refusal handled as data.
A human or automated supervisor approved a change whose defect was visible in the diff or in existing test output.
A dependency, host, runtime, or service behaved differently from its documented contract.

executionStages.definition: Reached only code paths that run without a model and without external writes: unit and structural tests, replay, dry runs.
Reached a run that invoked models against real inputs but discarded its output rather than delivering it.
Reached a run whose output was delivered to a consumer outside the repository.

statuses.definition: The defect was fixed and a named regression guard now fails if it returns.
The defect class is detected and recorded but the affected sites have not been rewritten; the guard blocks new instances only.
The behaviour was reviewed and deliberately kept; the entry exists so the budget count stays honest.

budget.statement: If two or more type-binding escapes reach shadow or live execution within a window of ten merged coordinator changes or sixty days, whichever comes first, the conditional typed control-plane pivot stops being optional and is scheduled as the next coordinator change.
budget.action: Schedule the typed control-plane pivot as the next coordinator change and record the decision transition in this ledger.

incidents.title: Empty fingerprint set returned as null
incidents.summary: A helper built a set of candidate fingerprints in a local hash set and returned it with a bare return. The pipeline enumerated the set, so an empty result arrived at the caller as null and a one-element result arrived as its single member. Callers that counted the result crashed or silently treated an empty set as an absent one.
incidents.detector: PSEN004 (local collection returned bare) in tools/Find-PowerShellEmptyNullHazard.ps1
incidents.regressionGuard: tools/Test-PowerShellBoundaryHardening.ps1 keeps the PSEN004 baseline at zero findings, so any new bare collection return blocks; tools/Test-ReviewerCollectionCardinality.ps1 exercises the zero and singleton variants of every inventoried hash-set field.

incidents.title: Anchor arrays nested one level deeper by array-subexpression wrapping
incidents.summary: Two call sites wrapped a helper that deliberately emits its collection as a single non-enumerated object in an array subexpression. Because the value crosses the pipeline as one object, the wrapper nested it instead of flattening it, producing a one-element array whose only element was the real array. Cross-file convention verification saw one anchor where there were none or many.
incidents.detector: PSEN011 (array subexpression wrapping a protected collection return) in tools/Find-PowerShellEmptyNullHazard.ps1
incidents.regressionGuard: PSEN011 fixtures in tools/testdata/boundary-hardening-analyzer.fixtures.ps1 assert both the hazard and its counterexample; the nesting property is proved directly by the protected-return escape shape in tools/Test-ReviewerCollectionCardinality.ps1.

incidents.title: Specialist capture plan arrays collapsed across the plan boundary
incidents.summary: Plan fields that carry a list of capture targets lost their array shape when a plan with a single target, or none, was serialised and read back. Downstream consumers indexed the field and received a character or a property instead of a target.
incidents.detector: Boundary variant harness in tools/Test-ReviewerCollectionCardinality.ps1 (specialistPlan stage, zero and singleton variants)
incidents.regressionGuard: Every specialistPlan collection field in tools/testdata/reviewer-collection-inventory.v1.json is exercised at zero, one, many, maximum, duplicate, null-versus-missing, and wrong-scalar.

incidents.title: Verifier JSON value shapes not preserved on round trip
incidents.summary: Verifier payload values changed shape when written and re-read: single-element arrays came back as bare values and absent collections came back as null rather than empty. Verdict comparison then treated two identical verdicts as different.
incidents.detector: Boundary variant harness in tools/Test-ReviewerCollectionCardinality.ps1 (verifierAssignment and verdict stages)
incidents.regressionGuard: src/Agents/reviewer/StageContract.ps1 normalises declared collection fields on write and fails closed on scalar-collapsed fields on read; tools/Test-ReviewerStageContract.ps1 asserts both directions.

incidents.title: Shared inventory return flattened at the boundary
incidents.summary: A shared inventory helper returned its rows through the pipeline, so an inventory with one row was indistinguishable from a bare row and an empty inventory from a missing one. Containment checks then anchored on the wrong root.
incidents.regressionGuard: tools/Test-ReviewerStageContract.ps1 asserts that the artifact inventory is returned non-enumerated at zero, one, and many artifacts and that the returned collection is read-only.

incidents.title: Source transport helper closures captured the wrong binding
incidents.summary: Script blocks referenced helper functions and script-scope variables by unqualified name and were invoked after the enclosing scope had moved on, so they observed a later value than the author intended.
incidents.regressionGuard: PSEN006 and PSEN010 fixtures assert detection of unqualified script-scope reads and of closures that call repository functions by name; explicit closure-state capture is property-tested in tools/Test-ReviewerCollectionCardinality.ps1.

incidents.title: Live source closure captured a mutated loop variable
incidents.summary: A closure created inside a loop read the loop variable rather than a copy of it, so every deferred invocation used the final iteration's value.
incidents.regressionGuard: Same as ESC-0006; the explicit closure-state capture property test asserts that a captured copy is immune to later mutation while an uncaptured reference is not.

incidents.title: Recovery reader closure captured state after reassignment
incidents.summary: A recovery path built a reader script block whose captured state was reassigned before the block ran, so recovery read from the wrong location.

incidents.title: Aggregate over an empty selection crashed under strict mode
incidents.summary: A byte total was computed by aggregating a filtered collection and reading the aggregate's sum property. When every item was withheld the filter produced nothing, the aggregate produced nothing, and reading the property threw under strict mode instead of yielding zero.
incidents.detector: PSEN003 (property read on a possibly-empty aggregate) in tools/Find-PowerShellEmptyNullHazard.ps1
incidents.regressionGuard: The zero variant of every inventoried numeric-bearing collection is exercised in tools/Test-ReviewerCollectionCardinality.ps1, and PSEN003 is part of the blocking boundary gate.

incidents.title: Second all-withheld aggregate crash in a sibling renderer
incidents.summary: The same empty-aggregate crash existed in a second renderer that the first fix did not cover, which is why the guard was subsequently tightened to reject the pattern rather than the instance.
incidents.regressionGuard: The tightened guard requires the numeric-zero form in the same block, so a sibling site cannot pass by accident.

incidents.title: Empty-aggregate guard accepted a same-block dominance loophole
incidents.summary: The first regression guard for the empty-aggregate class was written narrowly enough that a second instance of the same defect passed it. The guard, not the code, was the escape: review accepted a test that asserted the fix rather than the property.
incidents.detector: Review of the guard itself; recorded so the ledger counts guard escapes as escapes.
incidents.regressionGuard: Guards added by this hardening layer assert properties over an inventory rather than individual sites: the cardinality corpus is generated from tools/testdata/reviewer-collection-inventory.v1.json and the analyzer gate is baseline-diffed rather than site-listed.

incidents.title: Latent protected-return wrapping sites present in current code
incidents.summary: The rule introduced for ESC-0002 finds eleven further sites in current source and test code that wrap a protected collection return in an array subexpression. Each is the same nesting hazard; none has been rewritten in this change because mechanically rewriting unrelated code is out of scope for a prerequisite layer.
incidents.regressionGuard: The eleven sites are recorded in tools/testdata/powershell-boundary-baseline.v1.json with rationale; tools/Test-PowerShellBoundaryHardening.ps1 blocks any twelfth site.

gateObservations.observation: The gate produced no deliverable decision: every candidate was withheld or reconciled away, so the decision yield was zero per cent. The no-write invariant held throughout, which is why no incident in this ledger reached shadow or live execution.

decision.statement: Porting the coordinator's stage control plane to a typed, compiled host remains conditional. It is not taken in this change. It becomes mandatory if the escape budget above triggers; it may be reconsidered earlier if the prerequisites below prove insufficient to detect a new type-binding escape class.

prerequisites.title: Cardinality and property corpus over every collection-bearing stage contract
prerequisites.evidence: tools/testdata/reviewer-collection-inventory.v1.json inventories 236 collection fields across twelve stages; tools/Test-ReviewerCollectionCardinality.ps1 exercises all of them at seven cardinality variants, proves eleven escape shapes as properties, and runs nine sabotage checks; tools/testdata/reviewer-collection-cardinality-matrix.v1.json records coverage per field and does not claim full coverage.

prerequisites.title: Versioned file contract for stage child outputs
prerequisites.evidence: src/Agents/reviewer/StageContract.ps1 and src/Agents/reviewer/schemas/reviewer.stage-envelope.v1.json require a contract version and kind, write UTF-8 without a byte order mark to a caller-specified file, fix the JSON depth and form explicitly, and fail closed on unknown, missing, truncated, empty, scalar-collapsed, or stream-contaminated payloads; tools/Test-ReviewerStageContract.ps1 covers every rejection plus atomicity and the read-only inventory.

prerequisites.title: Boundary hardening analyzer with a blocking new-violation gate
prerequisites.evidence: tools/Find-PowerShellEmptyNullHazard.ps1 implements eleven rules; tools/Test-PowerShellBoundaryHardening.ps1 proves each rule against labelled fixtures and blocks any finding absent from tools/testdata/powershell-boundary-baseline.v1.json, whose entries carry per-rule rationale.

prerequisites.title: Escape ledger and budget with a registered trigger
prerequisites.evidence: This ledger, its schema, and tools/Test-EscapeLedger.ps1, which validates the schema, recomputes every count from the incident list, and re-evaluates the trigger.
